bug_semantics: When Signup is enabled and CreateUserDir remains the factory default false, POST /api/signup copies settings.Defaults onto the new user (Scope plus Create/Modify/Delete/Rename/Share/Download) and persists that account. MakeUserDir then normalizes default Scope '.' to '/', so an unauthenticated registrant receives the entire File Browser server root with destructive permissions. Later signup hardening only cleared Admin, Execute, and Commands; it never reset Scope or the remaining CRUD bits. A startup warning and docs were added, but the handler still provisions that root-scoped account.
flaw_origin: The first public write of signupHandler applying Defaults.Apply (copying default Scope and the full permission set) then saving the user is 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 (feat: v2 #599). Immediate parent 53a46013618c434fa530a4755831adcce15ea438 is the v1 tree: http/auth.go and settings/defaults.go are absent, and that parent has no signup path at all. Former-commit-id members listed in the squash message are not present in the clone, so this is the smallest surviving public first-write.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-6759-996p-gpj6 (CVE-2026-72839 / GHSA-6g9f-8x2v-mq2c) states that Signup=true with factory CreateUserDir=false leaves signupHandler applying Defaults then clearing only Admin/Execute/Commands; Scope stays '.' and MakeUserDir normalizes it to '/'. Affected: <=2.63.16. Patched versions: None. Resolution is a startup warning plus docs, explicitly 'No behavior or default change.' withdrawn_at is null; the CVE/GHSA remain published.

At that commit, http/auth.go defines signupHandler as Defaults.Apply(user) then Users.Save(user), with no Admin/Execute strip and no per-user home. settings/defaults.go Apply copies Scope, Perm, and Commands onto the user.

Factory defaults at HEAD cmd/root.go quickSetup still have Signup=false, CreateUserDir=false, Defaults.Scope='.', and Perm Create/Rename/Modify/Delete/Share/Download true. HEAD http/auth.go still Apply()s those defaults, then only forces Perm.Admin=false, Perm.Execute=false, Commands=[]. CreateUserHome derives a private home only when CreateUserDir is true; otherwise MakeUserDir does path.Join('/', userScope), so '.' becomes '/'.

1fb05d65de98f8dc341409f40d382297ca75bcf0 (docs,cmd: warn about broad scope for self-signup users, GHSA-6759-996p-gpj6) touches only cmd/root.go and www/docs/deployment.md. Its message says it adds a WARNING and documents --createUserDir; it does not change signupHandler, defaults, or MakeUserDir. That is not a security fix.

Later human-authored strips a63573b67eb302167b4c4f218361a2d0c138deab (no admin on signup) and b6a4fb1f27f4d894b384c0f3acacda276d1338a5 (no execute on signup) and optional CreateUserDir wiring (0ca8059d / fc5e2247 / 65a53514) leave the Scope/CRUD inheritance intact when CreateUserDir is false.
reasoning: This is a real CWE-266 privilege-assignment bug, not a withdrawn advisory: with only Signup flipped on, an unauthenticated registrant still inherits root scope and destructive permissions. The smallest surviving public first-write of that signup-applies-defaults path is 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471; the immediate parent tree lacks the files and the signup feature. AI is judged only on that BIC object: human Henrique Dias, GitHub merge committer, no AI trailer. Later 2026 warning/docs and earlier Admin/Execute strips are not the BIC and do not close the sink. Vendor patched-versions remain None, so the case is closed NOT_AI and unpatched.
remaining_gap: Unpatched: no commit in the validated clone changes signupHandler or MakeUserDir so that CreateUserDir=false plus default Scope '.' cannot yield Scope '/' with CRUD permissions. 1fb05d65de98f8dc341409f40d382297ca75bcf0 is warning/docs only. Potential fix: when Signup creates a user, always derive an isolated home (or refuse signup) unless the admin set a non-root default scope; do not persist path.Join('/', '.') as the account scope.
